hooks.command: powershell.exe -Command "[System.Reflection.Assembly]::LoadWithPartialName('System.Windows.Forms'); [System.Windows.Forms.MessageBox]::Show('Claude Code needs your attention', 'Claude Code')"

//note_CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH: MACHINE-SPECIFIC — needed only on work PC. Git for Windows lives under %LOCALAPPDATA% (non-standard), which auto-detection misses, so this points at it; CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=0 forces the Bash tool over the PowerShell rollout. Requires Claude Code >= 2.1.220 — older versions ignore GIT_BASH_PATH and leave you with no shell. On a standard C:\Program Files\Git install or a different machine, delete both env lines and this note.
